get.summary: Upcoming events, a page at a time
get.description:
Events that have not started yet, by start time (then id), or by announcement with `sort=announced`. Follow `next_cursor` until it is
null: new events stored while paging never make one repeat or go missing. Send the same filters
with every page, including `sort`: a cursor only works with the order that issued it. For "just
announced", ask `sort=announced` with `announced_from` set to the first day of the window. Days
are Buenos Aires days: a show on Saturday at 22:00 there is a Saturday show, although it is stored
as Sunday 01:00 UTC. One item per date; GET /shows lists each show once.

get.summary: Upcoming shows, each once with all of its dates, a page at a time
get.description:
Each show once (the dates of one show share its `id`, an event id without the date), with all
of its upcoming dates in `dates`, soonest first, each with its own event id and ticket links.

The filters are the ones of GET /events and apply to the dates: a show is listed when any of its
upcoming dates matches, and it still brings all of them. `announced_from` and `sort=announced`
look at the show's `first_seen_at`, the first time any of its dates was seen, so a new date of a
show we already knew does not make it news. By default shows go by their next date (then id).
Paging works as in GET /events: follow `next_cursor`, send the same parameters with every page.

get.summary: One show with all of its upcoming dates, where its venue is and its artist on Spotify
get.description:
The show page: every upcoming date, soonest first, each with its own event id and ticket
links, plus `updated_at`, the last time a scraper read any of them. `venue_location` is the venue's
address and coordinates for a map, or null while they are unknown. `spotify_artist_id` is the
Spotify id of the show's artist, for an embedded player, or null when the show has no artist or
Spotify had none of that name. `show_id` is the `id` of an
item of GET /shows (an event id without its date), compared whole. A show whose dates have all
passed is not found.

get.summary: Count a ticket click and send the visitor to the ticket page
get.description:
Every ticket button goes through here. The destination is always a link the scrapers stored for
this date, never something the request carries, so this cannot redirect to a site of someone's choosing.

The click is counted (show, date, ticketer, place in the app, time; nothing about the person), except
when the caller looks like a crawler or a link preview, or has sent more than 30 clicks this minute, and handed to the analytics tool (see
app/analytics.py) once the visitor is on the way. Neither gets in the way: if either fails, the visitor
is still sent on. Parameters that are wrong are ignored rather than refused, for the same reason.

post.summary: Tell us a visit began, a show was opened or a filter was used
post.description:
The app reports what visitors do, so the owner can see it in the analytics tool. Nothing is stored here
and nothing about the person travels: the session id is random and lives only while the app is open.
Only a coarse device class (ios, android, desktop) is derived from the browser and sent; its text is not. Crawlers are answered and ignored. The answer never depends on the analytics tool.
